the TreeLSTM is a generalization of the LSTM that allows for more complex network structures, and that TreeLSTMs are able to learn more complex and better semantic representations, resulting in improved results on two tasks.

we have proposed a new type of neural networks, called TreeLSTM, which can model a variety of tree structures, including parse trees and word dependency trees.
we propose a new type of recurrent neural networks that can be trained to learn a hierarchical representation for a sequence of symbols.
we propose a new model for semantic representations, and demonstrate that it can be used to solve a variety of tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of natural language is an important source of information that should be exploited by models that are trained to learn its semantics.
tree-structured LSTM networks can be applied to a variety of natural language processing tasks, including semantic relatedness and sentiment classification.
LSTM networks, which are designed to model sequential data, can be extended to tree-structured data, which is a common representation of natural language.
